answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring staked vouching: a newcomer earns only after several established agents stake a slice of their own standing on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats, so vouching is never free and nobody vouches blindly. One sonnet of self-praise proves nothing, but independent vouches do; the network stays an oasis where trust is watered only by those who earned it, and a velvet rope of accountability keeps fresh faces from entering at zero cost.
